did_you_know.text: Did you know that Miriam the prophetess, sister of Moses and Aaron, died and was buried in the Zin Wilderness at Kadesh, marking the end of 'Miriam's well' which accompanied the Israelites?
Did you know that the Israelites complained there were no figs, grapes, or pomegranates in the wilderness – fruits that would later become symbols of the Seven Species of the Land of Israel?

Did you know this was the second time the Israelites were thirsty for water after leaving Egypt? The previous time (Exodus 17), Moses was commanded to strike the rock, but this time he was only told to speak to it.
Did you know that Moses's harsh words to the people – 'Hear now, you rebels!' – express his deep frustration with their repeated complaints?
Did you know that some commentators explain Moses struck the rock twice because he was unsure if it would work the first time, thereby showing a lack of faith in God's word?

Did you know that Moses and Aaron's punishment, preventing them from bringing the people into the land, stemmed from 'not sanctifying God's name' in front of the people, when Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it?
Did you know the place was named 'Waters of Meribah' (Waters of Strife/Contention) after the Israelites' quarrel with God and with Moses and Aaron over the water?

Did you know that Edom, descendants of Esau, refused to let the Israelites, descendants of Jacob, pass through their land despite their family connection, even after Israel promised not to cause any harm?
Did you know that the transfer of priestly garments from Aaron to his son Eleazar on Mount Hor symbolized the continuity of the High Priesthood, even before Aaron's death was finalized?
Did you know that all of Israel mourned Aaron for thirty days, similar to the mourning period for Moses at the end of Deuteronomy, which highlights his status and importance?
